title: Static Members and Friends
summary: A **static member** belongs to the **class itself** and is shared by all its objects. A **friend** is a function or class that has been granted access to another class's private members.
ideas:
1. Give a `Bullet` class a static count of live bullets and a static `maxBullets` constant.
2. Add the factory functions `Color::fromHex(std::uint32_t)` and `Color::fromRgb(int, int, int)`.
3. Write a friend function `bool sameBalance(const Account& a, const Account& b)`.

cards.q: Can a static member function use non-static members?
cards.a: No. It has no `this` pointer, so it is not tied to any object.

cards.q: If `A` declares `B` a friend, can `A` access `B`'s private members?
How many copies of a static member variable exist if ten objects are created?
cards.a: One, shared by all of them.
